result:
I fixed the "Load more" bug in the shared paging helper, `src/server/repositories/_paging.ts`. Paging now returns every entry once, in the same order as one large page.

**Cause:** each list is sorted newest-first, with ties on the timestamp broken by id. But the "next page" filter only asked for rows strictly older than the last one shown. So when a page ended partway through a group recorded at the same moment, the rest of that group was skipped. Entries created gradually never share a timestamp, which is why only bulk imports, assignment bursts and bulk changes lost entries.

**Fix:** the next page now starts at rows that are strictly older, or recorded at the same moment with a smaller id. That matches the sort order exactly. Every repository list uses this helper, so the fix covers project issues, the notification inbox and the audit log, as well as comments, members, projects and search. Each list still keeps its workspace filter alongside this condition, so other workspaces' entries stay excluded.

**Also changed:** page sizes are now rounded down to a whole number between 1 and 100. Before, a fractional size would have produced an invalid database query.

**Verification:** the existing repository, service and lib tests pass (272 tests). I also wrote a throwaway check and deleted it afterwards. It gave 18 issues split across two workspaces the same timestamp, plus one later issue. Paging with sizes 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 returned exactly the same sequence as a single large page, with no other workspace's entries. No permanent test was added.
